comment: Latin has no verb of saying; 'they say' was an interpretive addition. New text renders 'quoniam quis audivit?' faithfully.
'triumph' is an added noun. The fix is faithful, though 'over my enemies' (super + accusative) would be closer than 'concerning'.
'Ne forte dicant' is a negative purpose clause continuing v.9's plea ('lest they say'), not a prohibition. Fix is faithful; 'et innotescat' correctly stays jussive.
'super filium hominis' depends on the verb elided from v.15 (respice/visita). Supplying 'look' restores that ellipsis without changing meaning; the new text is a dangling fragment in English.
'discedimus' is present indicative; 'will not depart' follows the Hebrew future. Fix is faithful.
'Sicut' governs 'laetantium omnium habitatio': the dwelling in Zion is like that of all who rejoice. The old text made the dwelling only apparently in Zion. New text matches the Latin (cf. Douay).
'et quaeremus' is a future indicative statement; 'so that we may seek' follows the Hebrew cohortative. Fix is faithful.
'dicet' is future indicative ('will say'); 'let all the people say' follows the Hebrew. Fix is faithful.
Psalter 'irritaverunt' (Greek parōxynan) means provoked; 'made void' is wrong here. Fix is faithful (Douay: 'provoked the counsel').
'jucundus' means pleasant or acceptable to others, not 'happy' (beatus). 'Pleasing' is accurate (Douay: 'Acceptable').
'fortium' means strong or vigorous; 'diligent' is the Hebrew charutzim. 'Strong' is faithful ('vigorous' would also be fine, given the contrast with 'remissa').
Same as 10:4: 'manus fortium' means the hand of the strong; 'diligent' is the Hebrew sense. Fix is faithful.
'disperdes' comes from disperdo (destroy utterly), not dispergo (scatter). 'Wipe out' is accurate.
'disperdet' means 'will destroy utterly', not 'scatter' (dispergo). Fix is faithful.
'vias peccatorum disperdet' means 'will destroy the ways of sinners' (Douay); 'scatter' confuses disperdo with dispergo.
'Inveniatur' is passive; the old active 'find' follows the Hebrew. 'Be found by' matches the Latin (Douay: 'be found by all thy enemies'). The second clause correctly stays active.
'educavit' comes from educare (reared, nourished), not educere (led out); 'led' follows the Hebrew. Fix is faithful (Douay: 'brought me up').
'et in opera manuum ejus' is a second object of 'intellexerunt' (Greek eis ta erga); the old text made it God's instrument. New text is faithful.
'salvationum' means saving acts or deliverances; 'victories' reflects the Hebrew yeshuot. Fix is faithful.
Adverbial 'et' meaning 'also, too' is standard Latin, and 'et hoc' here renders Hebrew gam zoh ('this also'). 'This too' is an accurate rendering.
The Latin name is 'Chusi'; 'Cush' is the Hebrew form, and it clashed with the Latin-based 'son of Jemini'. Fix is faithful.
'Consumetur' is future indicative; 'Let ... come to an end' follows the Hebrew jussive. Fix is faithful ('will be brought to an end' would be closer to the passive, but this is acceptable).
'occursus ... usque ad summum ejus' means his course runs as far as the height. 'meeting place is at' misrenders it and drops 'usque ad'. 'circuit reaches to' is acceptable (Douay: 'his circuit').
'Et erunt ut complaceant' is a future indicative statement; 'May ... be pleasing' follows the Hebrew jussive. Fix is faithful.
'dux' means leader or guide; 'companion' follows the Hebrew alluf. Fix is faithful (Douay: 'guide of her youth').
'Just as we wanted' paraphrases the Hebrew; the Latin has 'animae nostrae'. 'For our soul' is faithful. ('Euge' is strictly 'well done', but that wording is unchanged.)
'desit' (desum) means 'is lacking', the opposite of 'remains'. Fix is faithful (Douay: 'what is wanting to me').
'salutes' means salvations or deliverances; 'victories' is the Hebrew sense. This matches the 27:8 fix.

'intende' (Greek entene) is the verb for bending or stretching a bow, and v.6 continues with 'sagittae'. Many Latin commentators read 'intende [arcum]', so 'draw your bow' is defensible and not from the Hebrew (which has 'ride').
'narrate in turribus ejus' means 'tell in its towers' (Douay); 'tell of its towers' follows the Hebrew 'count its towers'. Fix is faithful.
'distribuite' means distribute or divide; 'distinguish' is not its meaning. Fix is faithful (Douay: 'distribute her houses').
'ad audiendam' (ad + gerundive) expresses purpose; 'as you hear' adds a temporal clause and 'you'. 'In order to hear' is literal and faithful ('so as to hear' would also work).
